diagrams.title: **One agent, three homes
diagrams.caption: **One agent, three homes.** The agent code barely changes; what changes is how it's woken up, how long it can run, what it remembers between requests, and how much of the plumbing you build yourself.

diagrams.caption: **Same code, different world.** Nothing in the agent's reasoning changed. What broke was everything around it: concurrency, resources, failure handling and visibility.

diagrams.title: **Five habits that don't survive production
diagrams.caption: **Five habits that don't survive production.** Each one has a production replacement; this section and the next show you how to put most of them in place.
diagrams.svg:

diagrams.title: **The workload picks the platform
diagrams.caption: **The workload picks the platform.** Short, independent and spiky points one way; long-lived, stateful and always-on points the other.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 400" aria-label="Two agents, two homes. The document analysis agent: a customer uploads a contract, the agent extracts key terms and flags risky clauses in about 30 seconds, traffic is unpredictable from 10 requests on a quiet Tuesday to 500 at quarter end, and nothing needs remembering between requests: a fit for serverless. The hospital scheduling agent: connected to health records, scheduling databases and provider calendars, with connections that are slow to set up, used around the clock, and booking an operating room takes several back-and-forth turns in one session: a fit for an always-on container." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">

diagrams.title: **Fifteen minutes is plenty, until it isn't
diagrams.caption: **Fifteen minutes is plenty, until it isn't.** Most single-agent tasks fit easily; multi-agent workflows with retries and slow calls can hit the wall.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 285" aria-label="The 15-minute ceiling. A normal contract finishes in under a minute. A 200-page contract needs many model calls and cross-references; twelve minutes in it is still going, and at 15 minutes Lambda stops the invocation and the work is lost. diagrams.title: **One stack, one delete
diagrams.caption: **One stack, one delete.** Because everything belongs to one CloudFormation stack, `sam delete` in `cleanup.sh` removes it all. (Leave the S3 bucket empty: a bucket with files in it can't be deleted.)
